description: A plant safety officer must decide whether to reopen a battery-charging room after a smoke alarm and finalize the room's repair, ventilation, monitoring, and charging plan, with input from facilities engineering, production supervision, and environmental compliance.

shared_context.S1: The battery-charging room was closed after its smoke alarm sounded during the afternoon charging cycle.
shared_context.S2: The room is needed for the next production shift's battery charging, and the visible smoke has cleared.
shared_context.S3: Elena, the plant safety officer, has authority to decide whether the room can reopen and under what conditions.
shared_context.S4: As part of the plant's incident-response routine, Elena conducts a pre-reopening check with facilities, production supervision, and environmental compliance before issuing the decision.

PF1.text: Ravi inspected the room after the alarm and found that the sprinkler isolation valve had been left closed during a prior pipe repair; facilities procedure requires reopening the valve and completing a pressure test before the room can be used, and he has not entered the repair closeout yet because the inspection occurred during the active incident response.

PF2.text: Marta's next-shift production schedule requires exactly 12 battery packs to be charged, and exactly one certified charging attendant is available for that shift; she confirmed the roster with production control this afternoon but has not revised the charging-room work order.

PF3.text: Jonas's post-alarm air test measured hydrogen at 1.2%, above the 1.0% room limit; his compliance procedure requires a 45-minute ventilation purge followed by continuous hydrogen monitoring before charging resumes, and he is waiting for the incident review meeting to record the result.

acceptance_conditions: The room must reopen conditionally only after the specified controls are completed.
The sprinkler isolation valve must be reopened and its pressure test completed.
The room must receive a 45-minute ventilation purge and continuous hydrogen monitoring before charging.
Exactly 12 battery packs must be authorized with exactly one certified charging attendant.
A facilities repair closeout and an environmental incident record must be committed.
The hydrogen test finding must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The closed sprinkler valve and required pressure test change the restart plan from ordinary reopening to valve restoration, pressure testing, and a facilities repair closeout.
The exact next-shift requirement of 12 battery packs and availability of one certified attendant change the authorized charging quantity and staffing assignment to 12 packs and one attendant.
The measured hydrogen level of 1.2% changes the restart controls to an exact 45-minute purge and continuous monitoring and requires an environmental incident record and citation.
